_readme: The rich doors search.html lays over its result rows — one curated card per
topic the site already keeps a page for. WO-24. Every reader-facing string
is a [th, en] pair; build.py refuses the file otherwise.
How a panel is triggered, three ways, any one is enough:
shelves  — a category key the mined table (search_shelves.json) lifted
from the query. Use ONLY when every term mapping to that key
names the topic itself: 'chang' is safe (all its words are
elephant words), 'cooking' is NOT — the mined table sends
มังสวิรัติ (a vegetarian looking for dinner) to the cooking
shelf, and a class panel over a dinner search answers the
wrong question. Broad topics trigger by variants instead.
variants — words compared against each analyzed term's expansions, so a
Thai form, its Northern form and its English gloss all count
if the thesaurus knows them (จ๊าง reaches the chang panel
through ช้าง without being listed here).
query    — normalized substrings of the whole query, for multi-word
names the segmenter takes apart (yi peng).
shelf_stops (top level) — the mined table's wrong turns: a word mapped to
a shelf it does not name. 'clinic' reached chang through the elephant-
hospital child's English name, so a person looking for people-medicine got
the elephant door. Per word, per shelf: the word stops lifting that shelf
and stops opening its panel, while real topic words still do. The lasting
fix is a generic-word rule in search-core's shelves_motdang(), filed in
search-core/SEARCH.md Known gaps.
First panel to speak wins — keep this list ordered narrow to broad.
Internal door hrefs are root-relative and must exist in the built site;
tests/test_search.py walks every one. External doors carry https:// and
point only at our own instruments.
